subtype: Approach: working backward from a target role and its listed skills [Thinking]
passage:
Hi Jeevan bhai,
Quick update. You told me to stop skimming fifty job posts and read three properly. So I picked three junior backend postings, from a logistics company, a small software firm and a hospital-software company. I copied their skill lists into a sheet and counted repeats: Python in all three, SQL in all three, REST APIs in all three, Docker in two, cloud basics in two. I already know Python and some SQL, so my real gaps are REST APIs and Docker. That is a much cleaner list than get better at coding. My plan before graduation: build one small API project, run it in a container and put it on my resume. Can I send you the project link when it is ready?
Thanks,
Arnab

qa.q: Which skills appeared in all three postings?
qa.a: Python, SQL and REST APIs appeared in all three.

qa.q: How does Arnab seem to feel about the new list of gaps?
qa.a: Arnab seems relieved and clearer, since it is a much cleaner list than get better at coding.

qa.q: What could Arnab do if the project gets stuck?
qa.a: Arnab could ask Jeevan or other seniors for help, and go back to the postings, since the focus stays on what employers repeat.

qa.q: How might Jeevan feel on receiving this update?
qa.a: Jeevan is probably pleased that the advice was used, and glad to be asked to look at the project link.

grounding: A final-year student picks three junior backend postings, lists the repeated skills and works backward to see which gaps matter most.
